newsitem.title: GERMANY: Intel hindered by weak Q2 Europe growth.
newsitem.headline: Intel hindered by weak Q2 Europe growth.

text.p: Intel Corp just beat expectations for second quarter results, but Europe stood out as a weak spot for the world's largest chip maker.
Second-quarter sales in Europe rose only three percent to $1.43 billion -- well off the company's worldwide sales growth rate of 29 percent.

Worldwide sales totaled $5.959 billion, as American sales surged 42 percent to $2.622 billion, Japanese sales rose 40 percent to $775 million and Asian-Pacific sales climbed 36 percent to $1.132 billion.
"The combination of seasonally lower demand and an inventory correction in Europe" caused the sluggish growth in that region, Intel said in a statement.
Intel was in the midst of a "massive" product transition, switching from older Pentium processors to new versions with MMX multimedia technology and its latest chip, the Pentium II.
Second-quarter sales in Europe fell short of the first-quarter's total, as did sales in Asia-Pacific. Sales in Japan and America rose sequentially, the company said.
In May Intel warned second quater results would not exceed those of the first quarter, blaming weak demand in Europe.
Intel reported earnings of 92 cents per share, just above the First Call consensus estimate of 90 cents per share.
